stories.title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration
summary: The trust hopes to restore the site, create new wildlife habitats and improve access to green space.

stories.title: How many sewage spills have happened in your part of Scotland?
summary: More than 76,000 sewage spills were recorded at overflow sites previously unmonitored by Scottish Water, BBC Scotland News analysis has found.

stories.title: Flood victim, 95, lived in Wetherspoons after her home was destroyed and died before she could return
summary: Jean Powell kept asking when she could go back to her flat, which was flooded when the River Monnow burst its banks.

stories.title: BBC Inside Science
summary: A weekly programme looking at the science that's changing our world.

stories.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
summary: Crows may be even smarter than we thought, and their brains are astonishingly fast.

Researchers at the University of Tübingen discovered that crows can make visual decisions twice as quickly as humans and monkeys, taking just 235 milliseconds on average to identify the direction of moving dots while maintaining remarkable accuracy.

stories.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant.
By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

stories.title: Nurdle impact to be researched for a year
summary: Research will be carried out on sea-birds and marine life following a microplastic spillage in July.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance confirms a key ingredient for life hidden in ancient Mars rocks
summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed complex organic carbon just beneath the surface of ancient Martian rocks, raising intriguing questions about the Red Planet's potential to have supported life.
The remarkable preservation of these compounds, along with similar discoveries thousands of miles away, suggests the building blocks of life may once have been widespread across Mars.

stories.title: A new treasure map reveals where Earth's lost prehistoric life may be hiding
summary: A sweeping analysis of 540 million years of marine fossils has revealed surprising gaps in our understanding of Earth's ancient life.
Scientists discovered that some of the greatest opportunities for finding previously unknown species lie in relatively recent geological periods, rather than the distant past.
By mapping unexplored fossil-rich regions around the world, researchers have created a powerful tool to guide future excavations.

stories.title: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'
summary: PM Andy Burnham was addressing delegates at the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey.

stories.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
summary: Researchers have discovered that a familiar tropical butterfly actually belongs to three nearly identical species, including one previously unknown to science.
Hidden ultraviolet wing patterns and DNA differences revealed the truth, leaving scientists puzzled about how the butterflies remain genetically separate despite living side by side.

stories.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
summary: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids.
Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation.
The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.

stories.title: Campaigners want more land protected from housing
summary: After parkland was safeguarded from development, residents want the council to change a housing plan.

stories.title: Art trail celebrates arrival of black bears at zoo
summary: Jersey Zoo says the art trail will celebrate the world's "largest inhabitants to its smallest.

stories.title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies
summary: Wales needs to grow more fruit and veg or it will be at the mercy of wars and climate change, one expert says.

stories.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
summary: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies.
Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.

stories.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
summary: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales.
The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.

stories.title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers
summary: The decline has been put down to severe restrictions placed on the substances' use.

stories.title: Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought
summary: Scientists have discovered that the first animals to venture onto land nearly 380 million years ago had surprisingly stiff necks, overturning a long-standing theory about evolution.
Rather than evolving to help animals turn their heads, necks may have emerged as part of the anatomical changes that allowed them to move using their front limbs.
